# Non-breaking Spaces in HTML

#### Course: Learn HTML

## Non-breaking Spaces in HTML

The major use of non-breaking space is to prevent automatic line break at a position. Let's see an example.

Consider this HTML code.

```html
<p>The World population as of 2022 has reached 7.837 billion.</p>
```

Normally, this code renders without any issue.

However, on smaller screens, the paragraph may break at an undesirable point, potentially separating the related information. For example,

```html
<p>
     The World population as of 2022 has reached 7.837 billion.
</p>

<!-- just for increasing font size -->
<style>
        p {
            font-size: 40px;
        }
</style>
```

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Browser Output

![Sentence without nbsp](data:image/png;base64,)

This time the paragraph breaks at 7.837 and billion. However, it's generally preferred to keep a number and its unit together.

To prevent this, we can use &nbsp; (non-breaking space) between 7.837 and billion. For example,

```html
<p>
    The World population as of 2022 has reached 7.837&nbsp;billion.

</p>

<!-- just for increasing font size -->
<style>
        p {
            font-size: 40px;
        }
</style>
```

Browser Output

![Sentence without nbsp](data:image/png;base64,)

As you can see, the paragraph now breaks at a more appropriate point, keeping the value and its unit together.
